```{r}
#| label: setup
# Load packages and define one shared chart style used by every figure
library(tidyverse)
library(nycflights13)

theme_report <- theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    plot.title       = element_text(colour = "#0b0b0b"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(colour = "#52514e"),
    axis.text        = element_text(colour = "#52514e"),
    strip.text       = element_text(colour = "#0b0b0b", face = "bold")
  )

# Plain-language table headers: code column name -> label shown in the report
column_labels <- c(
  table            = "Table",
  rows             = "Rows",
  columns          = "Columns",
  column           = "Column",
  n_missing        = "Missing",
  pct_missing      = "% missing",
  status           = "Status",
  n                = "Flights",
  pct              = "% of flights",
  n_flights        = "Flights",
  mean_arr_delay   = "Mean arrival delay (min)",
  median_arr_delay = "Median arrival delay (min)",
  mean_dep_delay   = "Mean dep. delay (min)",
  median_dep_delay = "Median dep. delay (min)",
  pct_late_15      = "% late >15 min",
  pct_cancelled    = "% cancelled",
  carrier          = "Code",
  name             = "Airline",
  origin           = "Airport",
  month            = "Month",
  variable         = "Weather measure",
  level            = "Condition",
  check            = "Check",
  count            = "Count"
)

# Print a table with readable headers and thousands separators (336,776).
# Any column without a label keeps its original name.
show_table <- function(data) {
  labels <- coalesce(unname(column_labels[names(data)]), names(data))
  knitr::kable(data, col.names = labels,
               format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
}
```

## Introduction

This report explores the **nycflights13** dataset: every flight that departed
New York City's three main airports (JFK, LaGuardia and Newark) in 2013, plus
related tables on airlines, airports, planes and hourly weather. It looks at
data quality first, then patterns in flight delays, then how weather relates
to delays and cancellations.

## 1. The data

The package contains five tables:

```{r}
#| label: table-sizes
# Put the five tables in a named list so each can be handled the same way
tables <- list(
  airlines = airlines,
  airports = airports,
  flights  = flights,
  planes   = planes,
  weather  = weather
)

# One row per table: its number of rows and columns
imap(tables, \(tbl, name) {
  tibble(table = name, rows = nrow(tbl), columns = ncol(tbl))
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  show_table()
```

Most columns are complete. The columns below have missing values:

```{r}
#| label: missing-values
# Count NAs in every column of every table, then keep only columns with gaps
imap(tables, \(tbl, name) {
  tbl |>
    summarise(across(everything(), \(x) sum(is.na(x)))) |>
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column",
                 values_to = "n_missing") |>
    mutate(pct_missing = round(n_missing / nrow(tbl) * 100, 1)) |>
    mutate(table = name, .before = 1)
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  filter(n_missing > 0) |>
  show_table()
```

The gaps in `flights` matter most: flights with no departure time are treated
as **cancelled** in the rest of this report. `planes$speed` and
`weather$wind_gust` are mostly empty, so they are not used.

## 2. Flight delays

### Flight status

```{r}
#| label: flight-status
# Label each flight: no dep_time = cancelled; departed but no arr_delay =
# diverted or incomplete record; everything else = completed
flight_status <- flights |>
  mutate(status = case_when(
    is.na(dep_time)  ~ "cancelled",
    is.na(arr_delay) ~ "no arrival data",
    .default         = "completed"
  ))

flight_status |>
  count(status) |>
  mutate(pct = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1)) |>
  show_table()

completed <- flight_status |>
  filter(status == "completed")
```

The rest of this section uses **arrival delay** for completed flights only.
A flight counts as *late* if it arrived more than 15 minutes behind schedule
(the FAA's definition). Negative delays mean the flight arrived early.

```{r}
#| label: delay-function
# The same delay statistics for any grouping (or none), rounded to 1 decimal
summarise_delays <- function(data, ...) {
  data |>
    group_by(...) |>
    summarise(
      n_flights        = n(),
      mean_arr_delay   = mean(arr_delay),
      median_arr_delay = median(arr_delay),
      pct_late_15      = mean(arr_delay > 15) * 100,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 1)))
}
```

### Overall

```{r}
#| label: delay-overall
summarise_delays(completed) |>
  show_table()
```

The median is well below the mean: most flights arrive on time or early, and a
smaller number of very late flights pull the average up.

### By airline

```{r}
#| label: delay-airline
# Add full airline names, worst average delay first
summarise_delays(completed, carrier) |>
  left_join(airlines, by = "carrier") |>
  relocate(name, .after = carrier) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_arr_delay)) |>
  show_table()
```

Airlines with only a few hundred flights (or fewer) have less reliable
averages than the large carriers.

### By origin airport

```{r}
#| label: delay-origin
summarise_delays(completed, origin) |>
  show_table()
```

### By month

```{r}
#| label: delay-month
summarise_delays(completed, month) |>
  show_table()
```

### By time of day

```{r}
#| label: delay-hour
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
# Drop hours with fewer than 100 flights so a handful of flights can't
# distort the line
by_hour <- summarise_delays(completed, hour) |>
  filter(n_flights >= 100)

ggplot(by_hour, aes(x = hour, y = mean_arr_delay)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "#c3c2b7", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_line(colour = "#2a78d6", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(colour = "#2a78d6", size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(5, 23, by = 2)) +
  labs(
    title    = "Average arrival delay by scheduled departure hour",
    subtitle = "Completed flights only",
    x        = "Scheduled departure hour (24-hour clock)",
    y        = "Mean arrival delay (minutes)"
  ) +
  theme_report
```

## 3. Weather and delays

Weather is recorded hourly at each of the three NYC airports, so this section
switches to **departure delay**. Each flight is matched to the weather at its
origin airport during its *scheduled* departure hour. Cancelled flights are
kept, because bad weather may be the reason they were cancelled.

```{r}
#| label: weather-join
# Clean weather: impossible wind speeds (> 100 mph) become NA; keep one
# reading per airport-hour as a safeguard (none were duplicated in testing)
weather_clean <- weather |>
  mutate(wind_speed = if_else(wind_speed > 100, NA, wind_speed)) |>
  select(origin, time_hour, precip, visib, wind_speed) |>
  distinct(origin, time_hour, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Match each flight to its origin airport's weather at the scheduled hour
flights_weather <- flights |>
  left_join(weather_clean, by = c("origin", "time_hour"),
            relationship = "many-to-one")

# Data-quality checks
tibble(
  check = c("Implausible wind speeds set to NA",
            "Flights with no matching weather reading"),
  count = c(sum(weather$wind_speed > 100, na.rm = TRUE),
            sum(is.na(flights_weather$visib)))
) |>
  show_table()
```

```{r}
#| label: weather-summary
# Put each weather measure into readable groups (each includes its lower edge)
flights_binned <- flights_weather |>
  mutate(
    precip_group = case_when(
      is.na(precip)  ~ NA,
      precip == 0    ~ "None",
      precip <= 0.1  ~ "Light (up to 0.10 in)",
      .default       = "Heavier (over 0.10 in)"
    ) |>
      factor(levels = c("None", "Light (up to 0.10 in)",
                        "Heavier (over 0.10 in)")),
    visib_group = cut(
      visib, breaks = c(-Inf, 1, 3, 10, Inf), right = FALSE,
      labels = c("Under 1 mi", "1-3 mi", "3-10 mi", "10 mi (clear)")
    ),
    wind_group = cut(
      wind_speed, breaks = c(-Inf, 10, 20, Inf), right = FALSE,
      labels = c("Under 10 mph", "10-20 mph", "20+ mph")
    )
  )

# Cancellations and departure-delay statistics for one weather grouping
summarise_by_weather <- function(data, group_col, variable_name) {
  data |>
    filter(!is.na({{ group_col }})) |>
    group_by(level = {{ group_col }}) |>
    summarise(
      n_flights        = n(),
      pct_cancelled    = mean(is.na(dep_time)) * 100,
      mean_dep_delay   = mean(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE),
      median_dep_delay = median(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE),
      pct_late_15      = mean(dep_delay > 15, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(variable = variable_name, level = as.character(level),
           .before = 1) |>
    mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 1)))
}

weather_summary <- bind_rows(
  summarise_by_weather(flights_binned, precip_group, "Precipitation"),
  summarise_by_weather(flights_binned, visib_group,  "Visibility"),
  summarise_by_weather(flights_binned, wind_group,   "Wind speed")
)

show_table(weather_summary)
```

```{r}
#| label: weather-chart
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.5
# One panel per weather measure, shared y-axis so bars are comparable
weather_summary |>
  mutate(level = fct_inorder(level)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = level, y = mean_dep_delay)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2a78d6", width = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "#c3c2b7", linewidth = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    title    = "Mean departure delay by weather at the origin airport",
    subtitle = "Weather at the scheduled departure hour",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Mean departure delay (minutes)"
  ) +
  theme_report +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x        = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1)
  )
```

## 4. Summary and caveats

**Main patterns**

- Most flights arrive on time or early; average delays are driven by a
  minority of very late flights.
- **Time of day** shows the clearest pattern: early-morning flights arrive
  early on average, and delays build steadily into the evening.
- Delays are worst in early summer and December, and lowest in autumn.
- **Precipitation** has the strongest link to delays and cancellations, then
  **low visibility**, then **wind**.

**Caveats**

- These are descriptive associations, not causes. Rain, low visibility and
  wind often occur together, and bad weather may cluster at times that are
  already busy, so their separate effects are not isolated here.
- Cancellations are inferred from a missing departure time; the data has no
  explicit cancellation flag.
- Weather is matched to the *scheduled* departure hour at the *origin*
  airport only; destination weather is not captured.
- Small airlines and rare weather conditions have fewer flights, so their
  figures are less certain.
